questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to North America, this was a great opportunity. It was important that the university tought some interesting courses, since I'm gonna spend 30 ects there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Reception was generally very friendly and useful. Sophomores are also very helpful and committed. You can always write emails to the different offices at uwo, they usually respond within a day.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When you check in they give you a map over campus and some advise to where the parties are and where the different offices are located. You can ask them anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I had to figure out how to get tested for covid on my own, since i was randomly selected for mandatory test in the airport. I spend the entire first day on this, and all the receptionist could do was give me a quicktest kit, which is not considered a legitimate test in this case.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I think all the residences were available but i got my first priority which was alumni house. This was somehow where almost all of the exchange and international students lived.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had our own kitchen (not all residence buildings have this). I opted out of meal plan but later regretted doing so, because almost all of the places to eat off campus also accept meal plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: No alcohol but weed is fine as long as you smoke it off campus. Dont hesitate to call the receptionist any time, they try to help with anything. Lock the doors when nobody is home, some of the rooms had stuff stolen in the last couple of weeks.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Horrible. It is impossible to see what courses are available in your term, at the time when you have to get them approved. So i had to guess. Then i get 9 courses approved just to find out later that only 3 of them are held. It takes up to 6 weeks to get anything approved at both universities so this is kind of tedious. Also, i only find one of these 3 course interesting and the rest were backup courses. As an exchange student from UCPH you have to study full time (4 courses in this case) so when i get there I'm still waiting for the last course to get approved. I had to go to the office and talk to some people before i got my fourth course, which was a course i didn't plan on taking.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You go to some online platform and select the courses you want to get approved. Then when they get approved you have to write to the international office that it is approved, and they will enroll you on your behalf. When choosing which courses you want to be enrolled in, you have to make sure the classes don't overlap. They give you a online tool for this but this can be challenging and make it even more difficult to take all the courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Didn't get much help until i got on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unsuccessful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Write to them and send them a list of the courses you have taken. This might shorten the time it takes to get stuff approved etc. but most importantly, i think that UCPH only shares your course transcript from when you sign up for studying abroad (which was november in my case i think) so if you take any courses in the next semester and even the last half of the first, they might not be on your transcript and therefore it can be difficult to get courses approved at UWO.
Also if you are studying physics, try and apply for mathematics, computerscience and/or astronomy courses also, since pure physics apparently isnt that popular/available at UWO.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally not that difficult, but sometimes a decent workload.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Since i had never taken any astronomy courses, i was struggling a bit in 3303A. The rest was fine.
2801A has a research project which make up almost half of the course. 30% of the grade on the project report was how good and fluent your English was.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It depends on your professor. Most of our professors was good at teaching. They all had very different styles.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ASTRONOM 3303A Galaxies
ASTRONOM 2801A Observing the Stars
PHYSICS 2110A Oscillations and Waves
PHYSICS 4662A Magnetic Resonance Imaging

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I only liked 4662A in MRI since i can use the part about nuclear magnetic resonance NRM. This was a course on my level. As was 3303A. 2110A was very easy since i knew most of it already and 2801A was almost high school level.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Tipping is a big thing and the bartender reminded us in the first week we were there. 
We travelled a lot so thats why my personal spending is high. Also i bought winter clothing but that was expected. 
Renting cars can be difficult to do cheap, especially if you are under 25.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Tipping, phone plans are notorious for being expensive in Canada. 
I am still not sure about whether the meal plan is worth it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. There is a lot of clubs at the university. You better sign up for those you like in the beginning of the semester since some of them get filled up quickly. Ask around or check online.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would not recommend the outdoor club unless you want to sign up as a driver (class 2 drivers license required??). I didn't get to go on a single trip outside London.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent cars and go somewhere. We drove to Chicago and back over a weekend (~6 hours drive). In reading week we went to Vancouver for like 9 days which was great. Sign up for some clubs on campus or go out in London. The nightlife is pretty good.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Not that difficult. Tipping was the hardest part to get used to.
Grocery shopping is not as easy, but no problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to bars and sign up for clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nightlife and openness to travellers from inside and outside of Canada.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Course registration is a mess so start early and dont be afraid to write to them. 
Sign up for a club or find someone to go out with or both. This is the best way to socialize. Once you have friends you can start traveling with them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Summer lasts for a long time and when winter hits it get very cold fast.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling and experiencing Canada.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Staying motivated to study. Saving money.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you want to save money you should plan ahead and buy tickets etc. early. Especially VIA rail and car rental.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
